rows.en: there was no end of poachers illegally hunting the whales for the black market,
rows.notes: review: refit: 'trying to capture ... illegally' -> 'illegally hunting'

rows.en: and the Zolan Star Patrol, guarding the whales, struggled with armed poachers.
rows.notes: The source says 'Zola's patrol unit'; rendered with the glossary name Zolan Star Patrol. | review: refit: 'which protected the Galaxy Whales' -> 'guarding the whales'; 'to deal with the' cut

rows.en: And now, once again this year, the season of the Galaxy Whales had come...
In an instant, the attack of the Boddole Zer Main Fleet left Earth in ruins.
Only one weapon could stand against the overwhelming might of the Zentradi:
rows.notes: Rows 85-86: the source is a noun fragment, then 'that was nothing but Minmay's song'. Recast so 85 carries a verb; the colon hands off to 86 on the same screen.

rows.en: Minmay's song, and nothing else.
If Zentradi soldiers, who had never known culture, were made to hear a song,
the shock would surely throw them into chaos.
Clinging to that faint hope, the Macross set out for the final battle.
Minmay's song was relayed by Vrlitwhai's flagship
to every ship in the Zentradi fleet.
Just as predicted, the Zentradi forces fell into chaos.
Staking humanity's fate, the Macross advanced on the heart of the enemy.
rows.notes: Source is historical present; narration put in past tense per brief. | review: refit: 'on this attack' and 'fleet' cut (source says the enemy's core)

rows.en: Its target: Supreme Commander Boddole Zer's flagship, the Fulbtzs-Berrentzs.
rows.notes: Short form of Golg Boddole Zer used, as the source uses the short form with his title. | review: refit: restructured

rows.en: With Minmay's song ringing out, the Macross plunged into the enemy flagship.
Boddole Zer fell before the Macross's all-out attack.
Having lost their command at the center, the Zentradi
no longer had the strength to stand against the Macross and Vrlitwhai's fleet.
And with the battle over, the Macross returned to Earth.
Two races created by the Protoculture,
the people of Earth and the Zentradi.
With the end of the war, the two began to walk a single path together.
But the embers of conflict between them had not yet completely died out...
Quamzin, unable to accept culture and refusing to coexist with Earth's people,
rows.notes: review: refit: 'live alongside the people of Earth' -> 'coexist with Earth's people'

rows.en: turned peaceful Macross City into a battlefield.
But the Macross rose again, and its main cannon set Quamzin's ship ablaze,
rows.notes: Source verb means 're-surfaced / rose again'; rendered 'rose into the air once more'. | review: refit: 'rose into the air once more' -> 'rose again'

rows.en: and Quamzin and his crew vanished into the flames.
And so Quamzin's rebellion came to an end.
The Macross was badly damaged in this battle, but meanwhile, a new spaceship
was being built: a colony ship to seek a new world beyond the solar system.
rows.notes: review: refit: second sentence merged with a colon

rows.en: %s and %s,
rows.notes: Used only by the SDF epilogue 2 (pointer table at file offset 0x31A9E4). Subject of 112-113, set off by commas around the 'to protect' clause.

rows.en: to protect humanity and its culture, joined the space colony fleet
rows.notes: 'Space emigrant fleet' rendered 'space colony fleet' (glossary: fleet / Long Distance Colony Fleet).

rows.en: and set out on a grand journey across the galaxy...
At Macross City's ceremony marking 30 years since the end of Space War I,
rows.notes: Source term is 'the interstellar war'; rendered Space War I per glossary. | review: refit: restructured

rows.en: Sharon Apple, who had already become self-aware,
hacked into the Macross's main computer
and seized control of Macross City's entire information network.
She even went so far as to put the people of the whole city under mind control.
Meanwhile, two fighters were heading for Macross City.
They were the YF-19 and YF-21, prototypes whose development was frozen.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'prototype fighters' -> 'prototypes' (row 119 says fighters)

rows.en: Sharon tried to destroy them with the X-9 Ghost drone and the Macross, but
rows.notes: Source writes the name as 'Ghost X-9'; glossary order X-9 Ghost used. | review: refit: 'eliminate the two machines' -> 'destroy them'; 'unmanned fighter' -> 'drone'

rows.en: thanks to their machines' astonishing power and the pilots' desperate stand,
rows.notes: review: refit: 'performance' -> 'power'; 'desperate resistance of their two pilots' -> 'pilots' desperate stand'

rows.en: the core of the information network was destroyed. Sharon was dead.
And so the Macross's rampage under Sharon Apple was brought to a halt.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'at the hands of' -> 'under'

rows.en: The incident was classified top secret, known only to a few insiders, but
rows.notes: review: refit: restructured

rows.en: it brought the danger of rogue unmanned fighters and artificial intelligence
rows.notes: Rows 126-127 recast so the incident ('it') brings the danger to light; source: 'the danger ... the incident became the trigger for it being recognised as a major problem'. | review: refit: 'running amok' -> 'rogue'

rows.en: to light as a serious problem.
In the end, the full-scale introduction of the Ghost was shelved,
and along with that, the development of manned fighters was resumed.
The nearly derailed development competition ended in victory for the YF-19,
rows.notes: review: refit: relative clause folded into adjective

rows.en: which was officially adopted as the VF-19 Excalibur.
rows.notes: VF-19 Excalibur: glossary only has the VF-19P Excalibur variant; base name taken from it.

rows.en: Meanwhile, the losing YF-21's capabilities were also highly rated,
rows.notes: review: refit: concessive clause folded into 'losing'

rows.en: and it was later given its chance to shine as the high-performance VF-22.
And as for the two who had flown those planes,
rows.notes: Cut so it works with the shared row 135 (no trailing comma there).

rows.en: %s and %s
rows.notes: SHARED STRING: the EBOOT pointer tables use this one string twice: Plus epilogue (134 -> 135 -> 136, table at file offset 0x31AB38) and Macross 7 epilogue (152 -> 135 -> 153, table at 0x31ABF8). Left without a trailing comma so both 'And as for the two who had flown those planes, %s and %s boarded...' and 'taking leave of the fleet, %s and %s vanished...' read correctly.

rows.en: boarded a ship for the far reaches of space to put their experience to use...
rows.notes: review: refit: 'bound for the farthest' -> 'for the far'

rows.en: The war against the Protodeviln, led by the immensely powerful Gepelnitchi,
rows.notes: Rows 137-138: source cuts as 'led by mighty Gepelnitchi' / 'the battle with the Protodeviln ended'. English moves 'the war against the Protodeviln' into 137; both rows are on the same screen.

rows.en: had come to an end.
Just as in Space War I,
it was the power of the songs of Basara Nekki and friends that ended the war.
rows.notes: Source: 'the power of song of Basara Nekki and the others'; rendered 'his comrades'. | review: refit: 'his comrades' -> 'friends'; 'brought the fighting to an end' -> 'ended the war'

rows.en: Once able to survive only by absorbing the Spiritia of other living things,
the Protodeviln, by singing together with Basara,
evolved into a race able to produce Spiritia on their own.
And so, with no more need to steal Spiritia, the Protodeviln
departed for some unknown, faraway corner of space.
Afterwards, Basara went on to make his mark as the vocalist of Fire Bomber
rows.notes: Source writes the band name in full-width capitals (FIRE BOMBER); glossary spelling Fire Bomber used.

rows.en: and became a singer whose voice thundered across the galaxy.
Yet the man himself had no interest whatsoever in such fame,
and he would end up wandering space alone. But that is another story.
Meanwhile, though the Macross 7 fleet had lost Battle 7,
it journeyed on through space, once again in search of a new planet to settle.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'continued its journey' -> 'journeyed on'

rows.en: And then, taking leave of the Macross 7 fleet, its battles now over,
rows.notes: On screen this is followed by the shared row 135 ('%s and %s') and then row 153, so the subject of 153 is the two player characters.

rows.en: vanished off somewhere, as if following after Basara...
rows.notes: Subject is supplied by the shared row 135, placed between 152 and 153 in the M7 epilogue pointer table.

rows.en: The giant Ranka was an illusion draped over
rows.notes: Rows 154-155: source cuts as 'the giant Ranka, [of the Battle Galaxy] placed under Grace's control' / 'was an illusion the Battle Galaxy wore'. English cut at the nearest natural point; same screen.

rows.en: the Battle Galaxy, which had been placed under Grace's control.
Ranka, who had been held captive inside the Galaxy,
rows.notes: 'the Galaxy' = Battle Galaxy, as in the source short form.

rows.en: regained consciousness thanks to Sheryl's song and Alto's voice.
But now it was Sheryl, her strength spent, who collapsed.
Alto and Ranka called out to Sheryl, trying to rouse her.
And then, a miracle happened.

uncertain: row 135: the string '%s and %s' is shown twice by the game (Plus epilogue after row 134, and Macross 7 epilogue between rows 152 and 153, verified in the decrypted EBOOT pointer tables). Written with no trailing comma so it fits both; rows 134, 152 and 153 were built around it. Anyone editing row 135 must check both epilogues.
rows 152-153: subject of 153 is the two player characters from the shared row 135, not anyone in rows 150-151.
row 146: source styles the band in full-width capitals 'FIRE BOMBER'; glossary spelling 'Fire Bomber' used. Switch if the project prefers the logo casing.
rows 137-138 and 154-155: English cut point differs slightly from the Japanese cut (the noun 'Protodeviln' / 'Battle Galaxy' sits in the other row); each pair is on the same screen.
row 82: 'Zola's patrol unit' mapped to the glossary entry Zolan Star Patrol.
row 114: 'interstellar war' rendered Space War I.
row 106: 'resurfaced / rose again' rendered 'rose into the air once more' (the Macross relaunching).
rows 85-86: noun-fragment pair recast as 'Only one weapon could stand against...: Minmay's song, and nothing else.'
missing_glossary: VF-19 Excalibur (row 131): only the VF-19P Excalibur Patrol Type is in mecha.json; used 'VF-19 Excalibur'.
VF-22 (row 133): only VF-22S / VF-22 (Wilbur) entries exist; used 'VF-22'.
Ghost (row 128): the generic drone programme; 'X-9 Ghost' (row 121) is in mecha.json, bare 'the Ghost' used here.
